Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggmap)
library(leaflet)

API Key

register_stadiamaps("bf91d81b-2ad3-45b1-a217-21bb0a13f297", write = FALSE)

Load the Data

For this homework, we will use the shark attack data to visualize where the attacks occurred. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

sharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA") %>% # pulling out NA locations
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude)) # converting longitude to numeric
  1. Use the range of the latitude and longitude to build an appropriate bounding box for your map.
sharks %>% 
  select(longitude, latitude) %>% 
  summary()
##    longitude         latitude    
##  Min.   :-124.7   Min.   :32.59  
##  1st Qu.:-123.1   1st Qu.:34.04  
##  Median :-122.0   Median :36.70  
##  Mean   :-121.4   Mean   :36.36  
##  3rd Qu.:-119.6   3rd Qu.:38.18  
##  Max.   :-117.1   Max.   :41.56
long_shark <- c(-124.7, -117.1)
lat_shark <- c(32.59, 41.56)
bbox_sharks <- make_bbox(long_shark, lat_shark, f=.03)
  1. Load a map from stamen in a terrain style projection and display the map.
map_sharks <- get_stadiamap(bbox_sharks, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom=7)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
ggmap(map_sharks) #display

  1. Build a map that overlays the recorded observations of shark attacks in California.
ggmap(map_sharks)+
  geom_point(data=sharks, aes(longitude, latitude), size=.5, color="black", alpha=.8)+
  labs(x="Longitude",y="Latitude",title="Observations of Shark Attacks in California")

  1. Build a map that only shows the fatalities.
ggmap(map_sharks)+
  geom_point(data=sharks %>% filter(injury == "fatal"), aes(longitude, latitude), size=.5, color="black", alpha=.8)+ 
  labs(x="Longitude",y="Latitude",title="Observations of Shark Attacks in California")

  1. Build the same map (fatalities only), but this time make it interactive using leaflet. Also, color the points red.
sharks %>% 
  summarise(
    lon_min=min(longitude, na.rm = T),
    lon_max=max(longitude, na.rm = T),
    lat_min=min(latitude, na.rm = T),
    lat_max=max(latitude, na.rm = T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   lon_min lon_max lat_min lat_max
##     <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1   -125.   -117.    32.6    41.6
lon_min <- -124.7267    
lon_max <- -117.1467    
lat_min <- 32.58833 
lat_max <- 41.56167 
fatal_sharks <- sharks %>% 
  filter(injury == "fatal")

leaflet(fatal_sharks) %>% 
  addProviderTiles(providers$Stadia.StamenTerrain) %>% 
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude, 
    lat = ~latitude,
    radius = 2,
    stroke = F,
    fillOpacity = .9,
    color = "red"
  ) %>% 
  addScaleBar(position="bottomleft") %>% 
  fitBounds(lng1 = lon_min, lat1 = lat_min,
            lng2 = lon_max, lat2 = lat_max)
  1. Which county has the highest number of recorded shark attacks? Make a map that only shows the attacks in this county. (hint: it may help improve the map if you remove duplicate locations, i.e. multiple attacks at the same location.)
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarise(county_attacks = sum(n())) %>% 
  arrange(desc(county_attacks)) %>% 
  head(n = 1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   county    county_attacks
##   <chr>              <int>
## 1 San Diego             24

San Diego has the highest # recorded shark attacks

#new Data with just San Diego shark attacks 
SD_sharks <- sharks %>% 
  filter(county == "San Diego") %>% 
  distinct(latitude, longitude)
SD_sharks %>% 
  summarise(
    lon_min=min(longitude, na.rm = T),
    lon_max=max(longitude, na.rm = T),
    lat_min=min(latitude, na.rm = T),
    lat_max=max(latitude, na.rm = T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   lon_min lon_max lat_min lat_max
##     <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1   -118.   -117.    32.6    33.4
sd_lon_min <- -118.1    
sd_lon_max <- -117.1467 
sd_lat_min <- 32.58833  
sd_lat_max <- 33.37
leaflet(SD_sharks) %>% 
  addProviderTiles(providers$Stadia.StamenTerrain) %>% 
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude, 
    lat = ~latitude,
    radius = 2,
    stroke = F,
    fillOpacity = .9,
    color = "red"
  ) %>% 
  addScaleBar(position="bottomleft") %>% 
  fitBounds(lng1 = sd_lon_min, lat1 = sd_lat_min,
            lng2 = sd_lon_max, lat2 = sd_lat_max)
